# Results -- Study 530 (Book-To-Market-Value) on real yfinance panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Protocol: annual
book-to-market quintile sort (long high-B/M value Q5, short low-B/M growth Q1), one-year
reporting lag, measured on a 40-name large-cap S&P 500 survivor basket. As-of **2026-06-27**.*

## Data stamp

| Frame | Shape | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|
| Book-to-market (fiscal-year x ticker) | 3 years × 40 tickers | `e42cf31942ef` |
| Forward total return (Y+1, ticker) | 3 years × 40 tickers | `fe6de140bdb3` |
| Signal years covered | 2022, 2023, 2024 (forward = signal + 1) | -- |

**Source:** yfinance `balance_sheet` (`Stockholders Equity` = book equity, `Ordinary Shares
Number` = share count) divided by `shares × fiscal-year-end adjusted close` = book-to-market;
forward return = the calendar-year-(Y+1) total return from auto-adjusted close (dividends
reinvested). Basket: 40 large-cap names spanning mega-cap growth, financials, energy,
industrials, healthcare and utilities -- chosen so the value sort has genuine cross-sectional
B/M dispersion (financials ~0.5-2.6 vs mega-cap growth ~0.02-0.4).

**DATA LIMITATION (named explicitly):** yfinance serves only ~4-5 annual balance sheets per
ticker. After aligning each fiscal-year B/M to a *complete* forward year (<= 2025), the real
panel collapses to **only 3 cross-sectional years** (2022/2023/2024 signal). The cross-section
is wide (40 names) but the time series is thin; the HAC *t*-stat on 3 annual hedge
observations is **low-powered by construction**. This is a hard ceiling of the free data
source, not a modelling choice -- and it is decisive for the verdict.

**Survivorship bias (named explicitly):** the basket is large-caps still trading in 2026,
projected backwards. Delisted value traps (the natural deep-value *long*) are absent, which
biases any apparent value premium *upward*. All magnitudes are upper-bound estimates.

## The honest test -- B/M quintile sort (long value, short growth)

Each year, the 40 names are cut into B/M quintiles. Q5 = highest book-to-market (cheap,
"value", the long leg); Q1 = lowest book-to-market (expensive, "growth", the short leg).
hedge = Q5 - Q1. Exactly one execution lag: the position is held for the full calendar year
that begins after the fiscal-year-Y 10-K is public.

| Statistic | Value |
|---|---|
| N years (annual hedge obs) | **3** (2022-2024 signal) |
| Hedge mean (Q5 value - Q1 growth) | **-5.62%/yr** |
| Hedge vol | 22.21%/yr |
| Hedge Sharpe | -0.253 |
| **HAC t-stat** | **-0.554** |
| Hit rate (years > 0) | 33.3% |
| Max drawdown | -13.3% |

- The value hedge earns **-5.62%/yr** at HAC *t* = **-0.554** -- not merely below the
  |*t*| >= 2 bar, but the **wrong sign**: over 2023-2025 cheap (high-B/M) names *trailed*
  expensive (low-B/M) growth names. This is the AI / mega-cap-growth era, when the value
  premium was famously absent.
- Value leg Q5 = **+26.23%/yr**, growth leg Q1 = **+31.85%/yr**, equal-weight universe =
  **+23.02%/yr**. Growth won the long-short over this window.

## Year-by-year hedge

| Signal year -> return year | Value Q5 | Growth Q1 | Hedge (Q5-Q1) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2022 -> 2023 | +10.8% | +33.8% | **-23.0%** |
| 2023 -> 2024 | +35.2% | +48.4% | **-13.3%** |
| 2024 -> 2025 | +32.7% | +13.3% | **+19.4%** |

Only the most recent year (2024 signal) was positive for value; the two prior years were
sharply negative as mega-cap growth ran.

## Placebo -- label-shuffle null

The B/M values are permuted *within each year* (destroying any real B/M->return link while
preserving the marginals); the mean hedge is recomputed over 2000 shuffles.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Real mean hedge | -5.62%/yr |
| Null mean (std) | -0.37%/yr (10.15%) |
| **Two-sided p-value** | **0.583** |

The real hedge sits comfortably inside the noise band: *p* = **0.58**. It is statistically
indistinguishable from a coin flip.

## Costs -- one-way bps x NAV x turnover + borrow on the short leg

| Component | Value |
|---|---|
| Avg annual turnover (two-sided) | 15.6% |
| Cost drag (10 bps one-way) | 0.03%/yr |
| Borrow drag (50 bps on short growth leg) | 0.50%/yr |
| **Gross** hedge mean | **-5.62%/yr** (t = -0.554) |
| **Net** hedge mean | **-6.15%/yr** (t = -0.606) |

Costs are small (turnover is low: large-cap B/M ranks are sticky), but they push an already
negative gross return further negative. Net of costs the value hedge loses **-6.15%/yr**.

## Robustness & synthetic positive control

**Synthetic control (faithful-engine / power check ONLY -- never cited for a real-tape stamp):**
plant a known HML premium and confirm the quintile engine recovers it, monotone in the premium.

| Planted premium | Recovered hedge | t-stat |
|--:|--:|--:|
| -0.05 | -13.47%/yr | -14.83 |
| 0.00 | -0.49%/yr | -0.54 |
| +0.05 | +12.49%/yr | +13.64 |
| +0.10 | +25.48%/yr | +27.30 |

The engine is faithful (monotone, near-zero under the null) and **seed-robust**: averaging
over 20 RNG seeds at a planted +5% premium, the synthetic *t* is **+12.9 (min +7.2, all >2)**;
under the null only 10% of seeds spuriously exceed |t|>2. So the negative real-tape result
reflects **the market over 2023-2025**, not a broken detector.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** Real hedge = **-5.62%/yr**, HAC *t* = **-0.554** (|t| << 2, and the
  *wrong sign*); label-shuffle placebo *p* = **0.583**. The canonical value premium is not
  merely below the bar on this tape -- it is absent and slightly negative. Literature support
  (Fama-French 1992) cannot upgrade a real-tape result that is insignificant *and* points the
  wrong way; per the house bar, that is NONE.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** Net of costs **-6.15%/yr**, Sharpe **-0.25**, and the entire
  test rests on **3 annual observations** -- there is nothing tradable here. The thin yfinance
  fundamental history makes any HAC inference low-powered by construction.
- **Did the canonical value premium survive on the modern survivor tape? -- BUSTED.** The
  most-pointed academic value factor, replicated honestly on a 40-name large-cap survivor
  basket over the only window yfinance fundamentals allow (2022-2024 signal), produced a
  *negative* premium -- exactly the post-2020 "value is dead" / mega-cap-growth regime. The
  faithful synthetic control proves the method works; the market simply did not pay value
  over this window.
